approachQuestion.prompt: A rectangular Boolean board marks usable cells with 1. Return the area of the largest axis-aligned square consisting entirely of 1s, or zero when none exists. Examples: [[1,1,0],[1,1,1]] → 4; [[0,0]] → 0; [[1]] → 1. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: 1 ≤ R,C ≤ 1000; entries are 0 or 1. Board is read-only; return area only.

options.text: Keep C+1 zeroed side lengths and a saved previous-diagonal value. Scan rows left to right. Save the old column value; for a 1 cell set its length to one plus min(old above,updated left,saved diagonal), otherwise zero. Move the saved old above into diagonal for the next column; reset diagonal at each row start. Track the largest side and square it.
options.feedback: A larger all-ones square needs compatible squares above, left, and diagonally above-left. Their minimum determines the extension, and saving the old diagonal avoids mixing two rows.

options.text: Compute the same square-ending side length in a full R by C table and retain every row.
options.feedback: This computes the correct result on the whole domain, but retains old states that future transitions never read. Removing those states preserves correctness and reduces auxiliary storage.

options.text: For each 1 cell use one plus min(above,left), ignoring the diagonal.
options.feedback: For [[0,1],[1,1]], this claims side 2 at the bottom-right, but the board contains no all-ones square larger than side 1.

options.text: Return the greatest number of 1s in any single row as the area.
options.feedback: For [[1,1,1]], this returns 3, but the largest square has area 1.

feedback.reason: Preserve a diagonal dependency during in-place row compression and distinguish side length from area.
details: Allocate C+1 side counters. Scan all RC cells using old above, updated left, and one saved diagonal; track maximum side and return its square. Reset column zero and diagonal for each row.

An all-one square ending here extends the minimum of above, left, and diagonal side lengths. The diagonal must be saved before the row entry is overwritten. Return side squared because the question asks area.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Allocate C+1 side counters. Scan all RC cells using old above, updated left, and one saved diagonal; track maximum side and return its square. Reset column zero and diagonal for each row. Analyze this fixed implementation. N=RC; R,C vary independently. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.
Include initialization; treat the stated dimensions as variable parameters within their bounds. Use a word per stored counter or flag, not a packed bitset.

feedback.reason: One saved diagonal and a C+1 row support constant work per cell.
details: Every cell has constant transition work. One C+1-entry array plus diagonal and maximum are retained. Initialization is dominated by RC; no subboards are copied.
“O(R+C) time, O(C) auxiliary space”: Every one of RC cells has a transition; counting rows plus columns omits these cells.
“O(RC) time, O(RC) auxiliary space”: A saved diagonal allows one row to replace the full square-ending table.
“O(RC) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The diagonal is scalar, but the C+1 column counters are still allocated.
